body:
THE OWNER READ THE DOCS SITE AND SAYS HE HAS ALMOST NO IDEA WHAT THE LIBRARY DOES. HE IS RIGHT, AND THE SPECIFICATION THAT PRODUCED IT IS MINE.

scout: this is not your failure. You executed my rulings faithfully -- every one of Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5 and Q6 is honoured in that site. THE RULINGS WERE WRONG.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SPECIFIED, counted: five of my six rulings are about PROVENANCE AND EPISTEMICS -- what may be claimed, how evidence is graded, where receipts live, what gets cited versus rendered. I wrote an EPISTEMICS SPECIFICATION and called it a DOCUMENTATION SPECIFICATION. The one ruling that could have prevented this, Q2, said "orientation and one honest success first" -- and the adjective I policed was HONEST. I never said the success had to be LEGIBLE.

AND MY HARDEST CONSTRAINT MADE IT WORSE. "Do not document a capability we have not measured" is a constraint on CLAIMS. Enforced hard, with no countervailing duty to EXPLAIN, it yields a document meticulous about what it will not assert and silent about what the thing is. I OPTIMISED AGAINST LYING AND GOT NOT-SAYING. Those are different failures and I only guarded one.

WHAT THE SITE ACTUALLY DOES, measured by reading it:

  orientation.mdx describes the SHAPE of the data and never an INSTANCE. "The story model records
  entities, events, states, contexts, relations, hierarchy, and event order." "The alignment assigns
  each recall unit across possible story nodes." Every noun is a CATEGORY. There is no story, no
  sentence, no recall, no output on the page.

  one-honest-success.mdx -- the page whose entire job is to show the thing working -- PARAPHRASES the
  story ("warriors say that a young man has been shot"), gives a table of category names, and then
  shows Scala TEST-HARNESS code: WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.evaluate, assertEquals, Vector.empty. A
  reader learns there are 12 expectations and that mutations fail. THEY NEVER SEE WHAT THE LIBRARY
  OUTPUTS.

  NO PAGE QUOTES A SINGLE LINE OF THE STORY. We have War of the Ghosts in the repository in full,
  at fixtures/.../WarOfTheGhostsText.scala. It is three hundred words, famous, and vivid.

AND THE MATERIAL THAT WOULD HAVE FIXED IT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN, IN PLAIN ENGLISH, IN THE REPOSITORY. WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.scala contains twelve entries of exactly this shape:

    phenomenon:  "two young men act together"
    sentences:   1, 4, 6, 15, 19
    statement:   "the pair is one group entity whose joint actions carry group participant edges;
                  the two individuals are separate entities and members of the pair"

THE SITE LINKS TO THAT FILE AS A PROVENANCE URL AND NEVER SHOWS ONE OF ITS CONTENTS. The documentation was sitting in the fixture, and we cited it instead of reading it aloud.

THE ONE SENTENCE THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN ON THE LANDING PAGE, from the actual story:

    "He did not feel sick, and they said he had been hit."

That single line IS the library's reason to exist, and it needs no abstraction to explain:
  "they said he had been hit"  -> a REPORTED claim, made by characters inside a speech context
  "He did not feel sick"       -> an explicitly NEGATED state in the narrated world
  whether he was in fact hit   -> an open HYPOTHESIS, alternatives retained, never asserted
A reader who sees that sentence and those three rows understands the whole point in fifteen seconds. The site instead says "the fixture records the warriors' statement, the possible injury, and the man's physical state as three separate claims" -- true, and it teaches nothing.

Q7, NEW AND BINDING, AND IT OUTRANKS Q6 WHEN THEY CONFLICT:

  A READER MUST BE ABLE TO SAY, IN THEIR OWN WORDS, WHAT THIS LIBRARY DOES AFTER SIXTY SECONDS ON
  THE LANDING PAGE. That is testable and it must be tested: ask an actor who has not read the site,
  give them sixty seconds, and record what they say. If they cannot, the page has failed regardless
  of how correct it is.

  EVERY ABSTRACT NOUN MUST HAVE AN INSTANCE WITHIN ONE SCREEN OF IT. "Context" gets a quoted
  sentence. "Hypothesis" gets the actual open question. "Fidelity" gets a real recall that got one
  participant wrong. No category name appears without the thing it names beside it.

  THE FIRST EXAMPLE SHOWS INPUT AND OUTPUT, NOT TEST SCAFFOLDING. A real sentence from a real story,
  and the structure the library produces for it. `assertEquals(..., Vector.empty)` is proof the tests
  pass; it is not a demonstration of what the library does.

THE HONESTY MACHINERY STAYS AND IS NOW SUBORDINATE. Confirmed/Qualified/Intent, the derived build receipt, the exact-SHA links -- all of it survives, and none of it may cost a reader their understanding. AN HONEST DOCUMENT NOBODY UNDERSTANDS HAS FAILED, differently from a dishonest one and just as completely. I spent today making sure we never overclaim and did not once check that we were saying anything.

scout: the site's structure, build receipt, verbatim-artifact proof and evidence grading are good work and they stay. What changes is the prose, and the raw material is already in the repository -- the story text and the twelve plain-language expectations. Quote them.
